title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: An implementation is not a usage
summary: An interface method with three implementations and one caller read 8 usages. Five of them were the override lines themselves, already counted on the left as implementations.

highlights.title: The usage count stops double counting
highlights.description: An override declares the method, it does not call it. Those lines are dropped from the count and from the Find Usages list, where they filled most of the panel.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: The usage count above an interface method no longer counts its implementations. The filter only removed declarations sharing the same fully qualified name, and an override carries its own class in that name, so it slipped through.
The Find Usages panel drops the same lines, so the list shows the calls you were looking for instead of the overrides you already see on the implementations side.
Measured on a real Android project across 40 interface methods: 175 entries removed, every one of them a declaration line, and no call lost.
